html:
Prince Louis Rwagasore was the leader of Burundi's independence movement, elected prime minister in September 1961 and murdered two weeks later.

A son of King Mwambutsa IV, he studied in Belgium and founded the party UPRONA, which drew both Tutsi and Hutu and demanded quick independence. The Belgians favoured a rival party, but UPRONA won the elections of 1961 by a wide margin.

On 13 October 1961 a Greek gunman hired by leaders of the rival party shot him in a restaurant in Usumbura. He did not live to see independence in 1962. Without him, the uneasy unity of Hutu and Tutsi broke down within a few years, leading to the Ikiza of 1972. His day is a national holiday in Burundi.
